candidate.answerReason: The acute angles sum to 90° and differ by 20°, giving measures 35° and 55°. The larger is 55°.

methods.label: Use a simple equation
methods.explanation: Let the two acute angles be \(x\) and \(x+20\). Then \(2x+20=90\), so \(x=35\), and the larger acute angle is \(55^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the Grade 8 complementary-angle property and an earlier simple equation of the form ax+b=c.

methods.label: Use the average and half the difference
methods.explanation: The two acute angles sum to \(90^\circ\), so their average is \(90^\circ\div2=45^\circ\). The larger and smaller measures lie equally far above and below their average. Their \(20^\circ\) difference is twice this distance, so the larger acute angle is \(45^\circ+20^\circ\div2=55^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the same geometric property with elementary averaging and halving, requiring no equation solving.
